title: Theseus: The Boy Under the Rock
subtitle: A hidden inheritance and a dangerous choice of road

plutarch.excerpt: to take from thence the tokens that Aegeus had left, and to sail to Athens. He without any difficulty set himself to the stone and lifted it up; but refused to take his journey by sea, though it was much the safer way

narrativeBlocks.title: A king hides his tokens
narrativeBlocks.body: Before returning to Athens, King Aegeus places his sword and sandals under a great rock at Troezen. His instruction to Aethra: if the child is a boy, let him grow up unnamed — and when he can lift the rock himself, send him to Athens with the tokens beneath it.

narrativeBlocks.title: Sixteen years later
narrativeBlocks.body: Theseus grows into the strongest youth in Troezen. Aethra finally tells him of the rock. He lifts it without difficulty and takes up the sword and sandals — proof of who his father is.

narrativeBlocks.title: The road nobody chooses
narrativeBlocks.body: Two ways to Athens: a short, safe voyage by sea, or the land road along the isthmus — infested with bandits who murder travellers. His mother and grandfather beg him to sail. Theseus refuses: a hero should arrive having done something worth remembering.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why the choice matters
narrativeBlocks.body: The road is not recklessness — it is Theseus deliberately imitating Heracles, the hero he admires, who cleared monsters rather than avoided them. He wants his first deeds to be public service, not safe passage.

narrativeBlocks.title: The pattern of a hero
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the archetypal hero's beginning: hidden parentage, a test of strength revealing the truth, then a deliberate choice of the hard path. Watch for the same shape in other heroes this week.

quiz.prompt: Why does Theseus choose the dangerous land road to Athens over the safe sea voyage?

choices.text: He wants to prove himself through deeds, like his model Heracles — arriving as a hero, not merely a passenger
The sea is enchanted against him
He does not know the sea route exists

quiz.explanation: Plutarch says Theseus refused the sea 'though it was much the safer way' — deliberately imitating Heracles by seeking trials, not avoiding them.

quiz.prompt: What did Aegeus hide under the rock at Troezen?

choices.text: His sword and sandals — tokens to prove Theseus's parentage when he was strong enough to lift it
A chest of gold for Theseus's inheritance
A letter naming Theseus his heir

quiz.explanation: Aegeus hid his sword and sandals; Theseus lifts the rock at sixteen and takes the tokens to Athens.
